gpuTelemetrySource: NVML utilization and temperature read from the same exact RTX 5090 Laptop device handle with native statuses and start/completion timestamps; CPU source explicitly excludes GPU and its WDDM activity gate
gpuSensorPlausibility: Positive through 125 C is only native sensor validity, never a workload thermal threshold; native errors or invalid values refuse the baseline
mode: Performance / Automatic; both exact 0D82 channels must return mode 2
workloadPathPolicy: Explicit runtime --workload-exe absolute path; exact basename, SHA256 and version remain fixed; path never exported
workloadOwnership: Operator launched and stopped; collector never launches or kills processes
arming: Refuse any preexisting target process. Bind exactly one new process after arm UTC by canonical expected installation path, hash, version, PID and creation time.
preArmProof: Fresh query-only paired Performance/Automatic, full 280 W, absent pad and independent GPU zero before ARMED; idle GPU and zero idle fans allowed. Retain the same actor for collection.
qualification: Three consecutive samples separated by at least 2 seconds of actual monotonic time of at least 80 percent NVML device GPU utilization; device-level load proxy, not process attribution
durationScope: Collection elapsed ends at the final 30-second wait. Fresh final process, utilization and eligibility checks have a separate recorded two-second verification budget.
requiredObservations: Exact process identity, full 280 W, absent pad, independent NVML and NVAPI zero offsets, positive CPU and active GPU temperatures, both positive fan RPM readings, paired Performance/Automatic
commands: Read only: 0D82 01010000/01020000; 078C 0000; 0D88 010100/010200, using existing exact 0528 admission
thermalPolicy: Export raw stock workload observations for subsequent human review; no inferred thermal limits or HyperBoost admission
failurePolicy: Stop queries on missing, stale or contradictory data, workload exit/replacement, load loss, cancellation or deadline. No restoration writes are needed because collector never writes. Wrapper separately restores its prepared service settings.
